If your equity falls below the soft edge margin requirement, **forced liquidation can happen right away.** You don't get the 48-hour window that applies when you drop below maintenance margin.

**What the soft edge is**
The help centre calls the soft edge margin "the threshold below which actual forced liquidation will occur. When your equity falls below the soft edge margin requirement, forced liquidation may occur immediately."
— *When will I be at risk of forced liquidation*, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_493

**How it compares with maintenance margin**
You're at risk of forced liquidation in any of these cases:
1. Your equity **stays below the maintenance margin for more than 48 hours**
2. Your equity **falls below the soft edge margin**, with no waiting period
3. Exercising or being assigned options near expiry could push your equity below the maintenance margin or soft edge

Being below maintenance (but still above the soft edge) starts the 48-hour clock. Being below the soft edge means liquidation can happen at any moment.
— Same article, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_493

**The soft edge can go up before weekends and holidays**
moomoo SG may, at its own discretion, raise the soft edge margin the day before a weekend or holiday. It usually comes back down on the first trading day afterwards. The help centre uses an example where the soft edge ratio is usually 20% but rises to 30% near the close on a Friday afternoon. In that example, an account worth $8,500 with $2,500 of equity is below maintenance but still above the normal soft edge, so it's safe from immediate liquidation. When the soft edge rises to 30% on Friday, it no longer meets the requirement and gets force-liquidated. These percentages are just the article's example, not moomoo's live rates for any particular stock.
— Same article, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_493

**How much gets sold**
It depends on your account. The goal of forced liquidation is to bring your equity back above the maintenance margin requirement, so only part of your positions might be closed. You can mark positions as "Liquidate Last," and moomoo will try to close other positions first. That's a preference, not a guarantee.
— *Will part of my positions be closed in case of forced liquidation*, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_494
— *What is Liquidate Last, and how does it affect forced liquidation?*, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_1446

**How to avoid it**
moomoo SG emails you and sends an app notification when your remaining liquidity drops below 10%, and again when your equity falls below the maintenance margin. The help centre lists two ways to avoid forced liquidation:
- **Deposit funds**, or
- **Close some of your open positions**

Either one keeps your equity above the maintenance margin. moomoo SG can still force-liquidate at any time if the market moves sharply.
— *How to avoid forced liquidation*, https://www.moomoo.com/sg/support/topic5_495

I can also check where your account stands right now against its maintenance and soft edge requirements, or test a price drop or weekend scenario.
